key_insight: The paper proposes a principled diffusion-based data assimilation framework that incorporates observation-error covariance explicitly via an ensemble Kalman update in clean-state space.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more Bayesian, computationally practical route to reconstructing turbulent flow fields from sparse measurements without relying on ad hoc balance parameters.
method: Generate clean-state flow estimates with a diffusion model.
Assimilate sparse observations using an ensemble Kalman update with prescribed observation-error covariance.
Use the resulting posterior samples to reconstruct turbulent fields from partial data.
evidence_signal: In Lorenz-63, the method achieved lower trajectory error and equation residual than other diffusion-based posterior samplers, and in Rayleigh-Bénard convection it matched large-scale DNS statistics with small-scale deviations.
watch_item: The reported ensemble underestimates posterior uncertainty, so uncertainty quantification may be overconfident in practice.
paper_title: Toward Principled Generative Data Assimilation of Turbulent Flows from Sparse Observations
